setlist.title: Why Don't We Do It In The Road?

first_in_archive: Why Don't We Do It In The Road?

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (4 reviews): Emerging from space, the Dew was thunderous, with Brent keeping up strong playing alongside Jerry; Called the highlight; Jerry's high notes gathered up loose ends from a dreamy space [19][23][26][30]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): The opener came out strong, though the rest of the first set was fairly uneventful [23]
- **Loser** (1 review): Described as very hot, with Brent worth listening for [26]
- **Help On The Way** (1 review): The Help->Slip->Frank sequence is singled out as great [24]
- **Slipknot!** (1 review): Help/Slip/Frank is tight yet loose and complex, barely holding together while finding a path through the Slipknot maze [27]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): A well-done Eyes; the fast mid-80s style isn't the reviewer's taste, but this one rocked [28]
- **Why Don't We Do It In The Road?** (1 review): Called a mind-blowing surprise; the reviewer says it was the first time the band played it [19]
- **Brokedown Palace** (1 review): A sweet Brokedown closed the show, following a powerful Dew [28]

## Setlist highlights

- **Why Don't We Do It In The Road?**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 7 archived performances [31]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-06-27.111477.beyer-senn.daweez.d5scott.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 20 songs; 167 min [1]
- **gd84-06-27.sbd.unknown.12929.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 169 min; rated 4.81/5 by 20 [2]. Said about its sound: Sound quality is superior, probably among the best the reviewer has heard [26]
- **gd1984-06-27.sbd.miller.repitch-87467.87658.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 164 min; rated 4.33/5 by 12 [4]
- **gd84-06-27.sbd.skankweed.4615.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 169 min; rated 4/5 by 10 [5]. Said about its sound: Jerry's voice is quite raspy at times, but the playing is confident and consistently good [21]
- **gd1984-06-27.163306.neumann.u87.akg414.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 19 songs; 170 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [6]
- **gd1984-06-27.148236.fob.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 163 min [8]

## Around the show

- Listener under the pavilion heard the loudest feedback he'd ever heard from the band, and suspected Healy was showing off for the Bear [20]
- Reviewer stood far back near the top of the bowl; the crowd went wild when Franklin's Tower broke loose after a long set break [23]
- Reviewer had fourth-row seats at the show [24]
- Reviewer recalls the first set as lackluster but calls the second set a killer, with Help/Slip/Franklin's building momentum [19]
- Consistent quality like this was rare among 1984 shows, according to the reviewer [21]
- Reviewer sees this show as a prime example of 1984's power, arguably Jerry's best playing despite his health struggles [25]
- Reviewer feels this trio dropped off playlists shortly after this show; the post-drums space and Dew are the set's best part [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-06-27.111477.beyer-senn.daweez.d5scott.flac16**: taped by Da Weez; transferred by D5scott; source: source: 2 Beyer M160 and 1 Sennheiser 421 microphones (15th row-center) > Nak MX100 w/2001 > Sony TCD5M - analog master cassettes; [1]
- **gd84-06-27.sbd.unknown.12929.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>PCM>C>Dat>CDR>Cool Edit 2000 Noise Filter>CDR>EAC>SHN [2]
- **gd1984-06-27.sbd.miller.repitch-87467.87658.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette -> Dat (48k) D [4]. Also: Nakamichi 300 to cassette master, then CD by Steve Ziemba; this source was pitch corrected [4]
- **gd84-06-27.sbd.skankweed.4615.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> MC> C> DAT> CDRx1> EAC> SHN [5]
- **gd1984-06-27.163306.neumann.u87.akg414.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob, Eaton, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Rob Eaton's Master Audience Cassettes; (2) Neumann U87's + (2) AKG 414's > Rolls MPX42 mixer > Sony D5M [6]. Also: Recorded by Rob Eaton, transferred and coordinated with Charlie Miller; a Sennheiser 421 source by Ron Pauline patches two sections [6]
- **gd1984-06-27.148236.fob.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Chris Hecht; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME80 mics > Sony D5M [8]

claims.text: Called a mind-blowing surprise; the reviewer says it was the first time the band played it
Emerging from space, the Dew was thunderous, with Brent keeping up strong playing alongside Jerry
Reviewer recalls the first set as lackluster but calls the second set a killer, with Help/Slip/Franklin's building momentum
Listener under the pavilion heard the loudest feedback he'd ever heard from the band, and suspected Healy was showing off for the Bear
Jerry's voice is quite raspy at times, but the playing is confident and consistently good
Consistent quality like this was rare among 1984 shows, according to the reviewer
The opener came out strong, though the rest of the first set was fairly uneventful
Called the highlight; Jerry's high notes gathered up loose ends from a dreamy space
Reviewer stood far back near the top of the bowl; the crowd went wild when Franklin's Tower broke loose after a long set break
Reviewer had fourth-row seats at the show
The Help->Slip->Frank sequence is singled out as great
Reviewer sees this show as a prime example of 1984's power, arguably Jerry's best playing despite his health struggles
Described as very hot, with Brent worth listening for
Trippy space into Dew is a rarity; the only other time was UVM 4/13/83, and this one is soulful and sweet
Sound quality is superior, probably among the best the reviewer has heard
Help/Slip/Frank is tight yet loose and complex, barely holding together while finding a path through the Slipknot maze
Reviewer feels this trio dropped off playlists shortly after this show; the post-drums space and Dew are the set's best part
A well-done Eyes; the fast mid-80s style isn't the reviewer's taste, but this one rocked
A sweet Brokedown closed the show, following a powerful Dew
Reviewer found the first night at the venue fun but not near this show's quality
Good Dew, with Brent bringing the organ to a climax at the end
Nakamichi 300 to cassette master, then CD by Steve Ziemba; this source was pitch corrected
Recorded by Rob Eaton, transferred and coordinated with Charlie Miller; a Sennheiser 421 source by Ron Pauline patches two sections
Master recording by Michael Hessberg, transferred by Charlie Miller; a Schoeps source patches the transitions and Drums
Taped with Beyer and Sennheiser microphones; the notes mention d5scott in the lineage
